The rape allegations against Trump: what we know and what is still being hidden

A new report from House Judiciary Committee Democrats contains new details about the Trump-Epstein relationship — and an alleged cover-up

Actual Article Body:
On Monday, House Judiciary Committee Democrats released a new staff report about President Trump’s alleged relationship with convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The report details allegations involving 11 women, including five of whom accuse “Trump of rape or sexual assault in Jeffrey Epstein’s close company or presence.”

The report is based on interviews conducted by Judiciary Committee staff, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) records, released documents, and survivor accounts. While the majority of the allegations included in the report were already public, it includes a new allegation that Trump raped a young model at a 1993 pageant.

“The report concludes that, based on the available evidence and witness testimony, Trump and Paolo Zampolli—who until recently served as a senior Trump Administration official and diplomat—may have been co-conspirators in Jeffrey Epstein’s conspiracy to traffic and abuse young women in the 1990s,” a press release states.

The report alleges that “Trump has lied about the nature and extent of his relationship with Epstein dozens of times.” For example, Trump has claimed that he kicked Epstein out of his club at Mar-a-Lago. But according to the report, members of Congress reviewed a 2009 document that reveals that Trump “stated unequivocally that Epstein ‘was never asked to leave’ Mar-a-Lago.” The file is redacted in public documents. Trump has also denied ever being on Epstein’s plane, but files show that Trump is listed on the plane’s flight logs “at least eight different times” throughout the 1990s.

Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee are now asking for a new independent investigation. The report calls for an independent special counsel to be appointed to investigate potential co-conspirators.

A press release argues that the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) “conflict of interest and obstruction make clear that Trump’s appointees cannot be trusted to pursue accountability.” The report alleges that the DOJ “actively obstructed the Epstein investigation into any co-conspirators, attempted to prevent the release of the Epstein files, and then released an incomplete and heavily redacted set to the public.”

The report also reveals that documents in the Epstein files allege that Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Deputy Attorney General at the time, “likely knew about certain survivors’ claims against” Trump when he interviewed Epstein co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell in prison. According to a transcript, Blanche, on at least three occasions, “directed Maxwell not to discuss” an individual whose report to the FBI implicated Trump, but whose allegations were not yet public. The report alleges that by doing so, Blanche “may have engaged in criminal obstruction of justice.”

“The bottom line: there is more than sufficient evidence to launch a criminal investigation,” the report states.

“The women who survived Epstein deserve to be heard, Congress must have the complete files required by law, and an independent special counsel must investigate Epstein’s co-conspirators and DOJ’s cover-up and ensure that state and foreign prosecutors have the evidence they need to pursue justice,” Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee Jamie Raskin (D-MD) said.

The White House has denied the allegations laid out in the new report. “None of these allegations are true. This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements,” a White House spokesperson told NBC News.

The report reveals new allegations against Trump from Beatrice Keul, a former Swiss model who participated in the Donald J. Trump American Dream Pageant in 1993 at age 24.

According to an interview she gave to committee staff, both Trump and Epstein introduced themselves to Keul when she arrived and promised to take care of things like her travel and education. Keul said Trump told her “I will take care of you” several times. So, when a Trump representative asked her to come to his room later in the day, she assumed he was following up on his promises to get her a visa and a New York University education.

Instead, Keul alleges that Trump raped her in a “brutal” assault that left her bleeding and covered in bruises. She said she went through the rest of the pageant in a “daze” because her passport had been taken from her and she did not want to raise alarms. After the pageant, she got her passport back and returned to Switzerland. She declined to participate in another Trump-sponsored pageant a few weeks later, but Trump called her and repeated his offer to take care of her.

In 2024, Keul told a different version of this story to the Daily Mail. At the time, she said when she arrived in Trump’s room, he “jumped” on her and began “grabbing and touching” her, but that ultimately she was able to hold him off. “I’m very tall, that’s what helped me a lot,” Keul said to the Daily Mail. The report does not say why Keul changed her story.

The report also includes the stories of four other women who have accused Trump of sexual assault.

Stacey Williams, a swimsuit model who dated Epstein in the early 1990s, has accused Trump of groping her when she and Epstein visited Trump’s office in 1993. According to CNN, three friends of Williams have separately confirmed that she told them about the incident, which Williams later described as “trophy hunting” for the two men.

Jill Harth, who recruited young models for Trump’s pageants, filed a lawsuit against Trump in 1997 claiming that he had “forcibly kissed, fondled, and restrained” her at a Mar-a-Lago party in 1993 when she was 31. The lawsuit also claimed that the same year, Trump had demanded Harth provide him with access to an 18-year-old contestant “whom Trump referred to as a ‘sex object.’” Harth’s lawsuit was resolved as a part of a settlement by Trump in a separate contractual suit brought against him by Harth’s then-partner.

A woman identified by the pseudonym “Katie Johnson” filed a lawsuit against Trump in 2016 accusing him of raping and sexually abusing her in 1994 at a party hosted by Epstein when she was 13 years old. According to DOJ documents, Johnson “was asked to strip down to her underwear and give a massage to Epstein” and “massage the penis of Epstein’s guest, Trump, with her hands.” Johnson later dropped the suit.

In 2019, a woman described as Jane Doe 4 came to the FBI with claims that in 1983, when she was 13 or 14 years old, she “bit [Trump] while performing oral sex” and that he “hit [her] in the face after she laughed about biting [him].”

Although Jane Doe 4’s claims have not been substantiated, the report alleges that the DOJ may be “still withholding a huge number of documents related to the allegations,” stating that the Post and Courier reported that it had reviewed FBI agents’ notes that contained new details about Jane Doe 4’s interview, but that those notes have been withheld by the DOJ for being “duplicative.”

In addition to these five women who claim to have been abused by Trump, the report also details the accounts of three Epstein survivors who believe that Trump participated in Epstein’s crimes.

Maria Farmer, a former assistant to Epstein who was abused by him, has said that on one occasion she went to meet Epstein in his office and Trump approached her there. But Epstein told Trump, “No, no. She’s not here for you,” before taking Trump to a different room. Farmer believed that there was a different young woman in that room waiting for Trump. She has said that she urged authorities to look into Trump decades ago. According to the report, Farmer’s “reports to FBI appear to be unlawfully omitted from the files released by DOJ pursuant to” the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA).

DOJ documents released under the EFTA detail other concerning incidents involving Trump. In one case, Trump was accused of agreeing with Epstein that one of Epstein’s victims, who was 14 at the time, was a “good one.” In another instance, a Jane Doe described how she was introduced to Trump by Maxwell and felt she was being offered to him for sex. She recalled Maxwell saying “things like, ‘Oh I think he likes you. Aren’t you lucky. This is great.’”

The report also provides three additional examples of women who seemed to have connections to Trump and Epstein. The first woman, Lauren Petrella, has never made accusations against Trump herself, but Harth’s lawsuit claimed that he sexually assaulted her. The other two women, Jane Does 5 and 6, spent time with Trump and Epstein during the 1990s, but have not accused Trump of any wrongdoing.

The multiple, credible, allegations that Trump raped women and girls should have been and should be banner headlines every day until he is finally forced from office and into a courtroom to answer the charges. Trump has been allowed to evade and obstruct justice for far too long. Republicans who defend him and screen him should be held to account as well.

If this was hard for me to read, I can only imagine what it's like for survivors of sexual assault and rape to have to relive their trauma. I'm preaching to the choir here, but Donald Trump is truly a grotesque individual, and the people and systems that have shielded him from true accountability deserve scrutiny in their own right.

By SAMANTHA LOREN, US POLITICAL REPORTER

Published:  07:35 AEDT, 28 October 2026   |  Updated:  07:43 AEDT, 28 October 2026

A 58-year-old Tennessee Republican running for a US House seat is blaming his 'youthful indiscretions' for sending unsolicited nude photos, with one sent as recently as five years ago.

State Senator Brent Taylor acknowledged sending nude photos in the past after the Nashville Scene reported Tuesday that multiple sources said they had received or seen the images.

One person told the publication they received an unsolicited nude photo from Taylor in 2021, when he was 53.

A second source independently corroborated the existence of nude photos.

'As I near 60 years old, the expiration date has come and gone on any of my youthful indiscretions,' Taylor told the outlet.

'Whatever story you think you've got, my wife is well aware of and we've worked through it a long time ago. My god and my wife have forgiven me, and I would consider everyone else doing the same.'

He acknowledged his past behavior, saying, 'All I can tell you is, in the past, I've been guilty of being a rounder, back in the day.'

A 'rounder' is slang for someone who regularly goes out partying, drinking, gambling or chasing women.

Tennessee State Senator Brent Taylor was accused by multiple people of sending unsolicited nude photos as recently as five years ago. Taylor has been married to his wife, Kimberly for over 30 years

'As I near 60 years old, the expiration date has come and gone on any of my youthful indiscretions,' Taylor told the Nashville Scene

President Donald Trump endorsed Taylor in July, calling him a 'Highly Respected State Senator' and promising voters that he would 'NEVER LET YOU DOWN'

The allegations raise questions about the private conduct of a Republican who has presented himself as a conservative Christian, devoted husband and father.

His Democratic opponent, Representative Justin Pearson, called the act disturbing.

In a post on X, he wrote:

'I'm disturbed to learn of Brent Taylor's pattern of sending unsolicited nude photos to multiple women.

The fact that he would dismiss his behavior as 'youthful indiscretions' despite it happening recently, in his fifties, & while he held government office is ridiculous,' he added.

'This is the type of predatory behavior that needs to be rooted out of our society and politics,' Taylor continued.

He accused Taylor and President Trump of abusing their power and escaping accountability, arguing that Tennessee needs leaders who respect women rather than sexually harass, expose themselves to, or exploit them.

Taylor, who has served in the Tennessee Senate since November 2022, won the Republican nomination for Tennessee's 9th Congressional District in August.

Pearson and Taylor are competing for a redistricted seat that was abandoned by Democratic Rep. Steve Cohen.

He announced last spring that he would not seek reelection after Tennessee Republicans split his Memphis-based district among three redrawn districts

Trump endorsed Taylor in July, calling him a 'Highly Respected State Senator.'

Trump praised Taylor for his conservative credentials and pledged that he would work to secure the border, combat migrant crime, support law enforcement and advance the president's agenda.

Taylor has also secured backing from some of the Republican Party's most senior figures, including Tennessee Senators Marsha Blackburn and Bill Hagerty, who have praised his candidacy and his focus on public safety and fighting crime.

Taylor's campaign biography describes a family man whose wife, Kimberly, has stood by him through more than 30 years of marriage.

The couple have two adult children.

He and his wife live in Eads, Tennessee, and are active members of Trinity Baptist Church in Cordova.

The Daily Mail reached out to Taylor for comment.
